statement: Cryptographic Signer identity and semantic Author identity are distinct concepts.
Valid author delegation may cause an operation signed by a delegate to be evaluated semantically as authored by the grantor.
A direct Permission Grant authorizes the grantee acting as itself; it does not by itself rewrite the semantic Author to the grantor.

Historical authorization is evaluated against the authority state relevant to the signed operation time; a later grant revocation does not automatically invalidate an operation that was authorized earlier.
Continuing disclosure mechanisms may require current authorization even when historical admission remains valid.
Replicated, forwarded, or replayed messages must pass normal destination admission and authorization; provenance from another DWN is not an authorization bypass.
